newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: "FIGHTING IRISH" WIN AS US FOOTBALL INVADES DUBLIN.
newsitem.headline: "FIGHTING IRISH" WIN AS US FOOTBALL INVADES DUBLIN.

text.p: The home of Gaelic Football was taken over by American Football on Saturday as cheerleaders, brass bands and thousands of U.S. fans invaded Dublin for a match between Notre Dame University and the U.S. Naval Academy.

In front of 40,000 spectators, Notre Dame -- based in South Bend, Indiana and nicknamed the "fighting Irish" because of their Irish-American heritage -- beat Navy 54-27 in Dublin's Croke Park, Ireland's national Gaelic Games stadium. Navy is based in Annapolis, Maryland.
More than 15,000 fans travelled from the United States for the fixture, filling Dublin's hotels -- and pubs -- to capacity.
It was the the biggest American Football match to be played outside the United States this year, and the first time ever that a non-Gaelic match was allowed in Croke Park.
For the first time in history, the stadium's hallowed turf played host to cheerleaders, dancing mascots and marching bands -- as well as 20,000 hot dogs.
During the match, Notre Dame fans were rallied by the team's mascot -- a man dressed as an Irish leprechaun -- while the Navy paraded a goat up and down the sidelines to inspire their supporters.
The Navy's original goat was banned from Ireland due to quarantine regulations, but a substitute Irish goat was found to act as the team's mascot.
